newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar opens stronger, expected to rally.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar opens stronger, expected to rally.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened stronger at C$1.3660 (US$0.7320) on Friday as the currency continued to benefit from signs that the Bank of Canada is preparing to tighten monetary policy, traders said. * They said yesterday's huge Canada dollar rally continued overnight in overseas trading as investors pushed the currency past the C$1.3685 (US$0.7307) technical level.
Traders said investors in London were continuing to buy heavy volumes of the Canadian dollar in early morning trading.
Yesterday, Canada's dollar staged its biggest one-day rally since the 1994 Quebec provincial election, gaining more than one U.S. cent against the U.S. dollar.

The rally was sparked by Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen who said during a press conference following release of the bank's semi-annual monetary policy report that there was a need for a less stimulative monetary policy.
Analysts agreed that Thiessen's remarks helped underpin a market belief that the Canadian dollar was undervalued.
"Given the risks inherent in the currency, the dollar is undervalued," said Michael Gregory, economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers.
"But you have to keep in mind that the currency was trading slightly below C$1.3600 (US$0.7352) back in mid-March before all the fears of (U.S.) Fed tightening took hold," Gregory said.
"I expect we're going to drift down to C$1.3600 (US$0.7352) and then, depending on how the economy fares and the prospects of fractual rate hikes, we begin to march ahead," Gregory said.

The U.S. Federal Reserve will meet on Tuesday to decide whether to tinker with interest rates. The last Fed hike on March 25 triggered a broad-based sell-off of Canadian securities and a slide in the value of the Canada dollar.
Traders said there could be some profit-taking and selling of the Canada dollar overseas on Monday, when Canadian markets are closed for the Victoria Day holiday.
"We're certainly vulnerable to a small sell-off," one trader said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 84.60 yen from Thursday's close of 84.40 and jumped to 1.2457 marks from Thursday's 1.2367 marks.
